name: Avalanches
description: Rapid movement of snow down a slope, capable of burying or sweeping away climbers with little warning.
prevention: Check avalanche forecasts, avoid loaded slopes after fresh snowfall, and carry a transceiver, probe, and shovel.

name: Hypothermia
description: A dangerous drop in core body temperature caused by cold, wind, and wet conditions.
prevention: Layer clothing appropriately, stay dry, eat regularly, and recognise early signs such as shivering and confusion.

name: Altitude Sickness
description: A range of illnesses caused by reduced oxygen at elevation, from mild headaches to life-threatening fluid in the lungs or brain.
prevention: Ascend gradually, follow a proper acclimatisation schedule, and descend immediately if serious symptoms appear.

name: Rockfall
description: Loose rock dislodged by weather, wildlife, or other climbers can fall with little warning on many mountain routes.
prevention: Wear a helmet, move efficiently through exposed gullies, and avoid climbing directly below other parties.

name: Crevasses
description: Deep fractures in glacier ice, often hidden by snow bridges, that pose a serious fall hazard.
prevention: Travel roped on glaciers, probe suspect snow bridges, and carry crevasse rescue equipment at all times.

name: Extreme Weather
description: Sudden storms, high winds, and whiteout conditions can develop quickly in mountain environments.
prevention: Monitor forecasts closely, set turnaround times, and be willing to abandon a summit attempt when conditions deteriorate.

name: Falling Ice
description: Seracs and hanging glaciers can collapse without warning, sending large blocks of ice down a route.
prevention: Minimise time spent beneath serac zones and move through such terrain during the coldest, most stable hours.

name: Navigation Errors
description: Poor visibility and featureless terrain can lead a team off route, increasing exposure to other hazards.
prevention: Carry map, compass, and GPS backups, record waypoints, and turn back early when visibility drops.
